facts.text: In mid-October heavy blowdown lay across the slope from about 2,200 to 4,200 ft, slowing both the climb and the descent.
In mid-October a dusting of snow on the heather benches above 5,300 ft made footing slick.
After the leftward traverse near 5,360 ft, stay low rather than high; climbing high there leads onto a steep slab.
Near the top, keep to the west side of the ridge past the rock tower for longer; rejoining the crest early makes the final scramble harder.
about 3 liters of water (none on the route in late September)
